otel_adi: DoubleTree by Hilton Bodrum Isil Club Ultra All Inclusive Resort
yorum: The worst hotel we've ever stayed in in Turkey. We drove the entire Turkish coast from Mersin to Izmir. And we had to "check off" Bodrum as well. We decided to stay at this hotel and paid 41,000 rubles for one night (which is a decent amount for Turkey, but apparently not for Bodrum). The hotel is not 5* at all. Food is a 3-star, service is a 4-star. The food is simply really bad! It feels like you're in a 3-star hotel! You have a choice for dinner: either overcooked meat or overcooked meat, and to avoid any problems, you end up choosing the overcooked grilled fish... Mashed potatoes with peppers. There are no simple, understandable dishes. Some kind of stew and a mishmash of chicken and vegetables. You could overlook all this, but the food is truly terrible. You literally can't put together even one dish for dinner. I'm not even talking about seafood. There was nothing like that here. We ate peaches. Patisserie is desserts from the cafeteria... the ice cream is decent. We didn't have time for lunch, so we tried the snack bar. It was very bad food... spicy, overdried chicken. Or shawarma. The only thing that's okay is pizza. From 5 to 6 pm is "BBQ time." What do you expect from a 5-star hotel? Well, for example, grilled fish or meat. No, it's a Turkish burger, just one. That's all. Breakfasts are acceptable, they have what you need, but nothing fancy. Beach. There's no beach as such, just sun loungers on the pier and on the grass above the pier, but finding them is a hassle. Vacationers throw down their towels and leave, and no one keeps an eye on them. Entrance to the sea is convenient from the pier. The sea is a murky puddle, like swimming in a lake in the Leningrad region. We love snorkeling; there are lots of fish, but you can't really see them through the murky water. And I always wondered who these people were, coming to this hotel specifically for their one and only vacation. Sure, we were just passing through and made a mistake with the hotel—it happens, but why come here for your entire vacation when, for the same money, in Kemer, for example, you could get a super hotel with excellent food and pristine sea and nature? Hot? Then Ölüdeniz. But why Bodrum? As far as I understand, 40,000 a night (what we paid, not including flights!) is very low for Bodrum, and for that price, "thank you for the bed" is a welcome surprise 😄 but we didn't know that. We could have stayed at a small boutique hotel with breakfast in the city center and then visited different beaches. But if you want all-inclusive, choose a significantly more expensive hotel. Customer: Mostly Turkish. Everything's fine, but! Their smoking culture is outrageous. So, coming to the beach, dragging a sun lounger right up to it, and starting smoking nonstop is par for the course. It's disgusting and unpleasant, and we had to leave. yorum: For less than 900 RMB, including three meals, the price is quite reasonable. The food isn't particularly outstanding, but in Turkey where food is generally unpalatable, the all-inclusive meals at the hotel suddenly seem quite filling. Even the Hilton DoubleTree maintains its standards, boasting a private beach where you can snorkel and swim in clear water. There's also a swimming pool, and the rooms are individual villas nestled in the garden. In addition to three meals a day, there's afternoon tea with burgers, coffee, and pizza—eat as much as you like. This is perfect for a few days' stay where you can completely relax and not plan to go anywhere. It's especially great for those traveling by car because parking is incredibly easy.
